clue.text: Gambles crossing street of city in riots

indicators.note: the gambling word straddles, or crosses over, the street-and-city pair, holding it inside

parts.note: to dice is to gamble, so gambles gives dices
urban means of or belonging to a city

explanation.surface: Betting on the streets of a city sparks unrest and riots.
explanation.definitionFit: Riots are outbreaks of public disorder, which is what disturbances means in the plural sense.

clue.text: Grey, say, up above, cooler underground

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the abbreviation for say is written bottom to top

parts.note: EG, exempli gratia, means for example or say
on means above, resting on top of

explanation.surface: Grey Earl, say, upstairs, with a cooler place underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' is slang for a prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooler is slang for a prison, and a dungeon is a cell beneath a castle.

clue.text: Banks incorporating current accounts

indicators.note: incorporating means the banks word takes the current symbol into its body

parts.note: to bank is to save or store, so banks gives stores
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: Banks taking current accounts into their books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current accounts' looks like banking; 'accounts' are tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts are narratives or tales, the same as stories.

clue.text: First out of bed tormented me with strop

parts.note: up means risen, out of bed

indicators.note: tormented means twisted and tortured, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: The first one up was in a temper and tormented me.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppermost means highest or foremost, so first in rank or position.

clue.text: Reserve seat?

definitions.meaning: in sport, the substitutes collectively, who wait to be called on
a long seat for several people

explanation.surface: Asking whether a seat can be booked in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: The substitutes sit on a long seat beside the pitch, so the same word names both the reserves and the seat.

clue.text: Chewed part of pen leaked

parts.note: the nib is the writing point of a pen
bled means leaked, as colour or ink bleeds

explanation.surface: Someone chewed a pen and it leaked.
explanation.definitionFit: To nibble is to bite at in small mouthfuls, a gentle way of chewing.

clue.text: Groom's plea getting in tangle with tie

indicators.note: letters in a tangle are knotted up, so plea and tie are muddled together into a new order

explanation.surface: A bridegroom's plea as he struggles to tie his tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' is the wedding man; here it is the verb meaning to tidy one's body.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom is to tidy one's appearance, and removing body hair is one form of such personal grooming.

clue.text: Crew's excited, gathering in monarch's smashing boat

indicators.note: gathering means the jumbled crew letters gather the trendy word into their midst
excited means stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: hip and in both mean fashionable
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: An excited crew gather in the king's boat as it is smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrecking a vessel is the act of smashing a boat, so the gerund matches the phrase.

clue.text: Run mobile phone holding company

indicators.note: holding means the rearranged phone letters keep the company abbreviation inside them
mobile means able to move about, so the letters of phone are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to manage a mobile phone holding company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like a verb meaning manage; it is a noun, the enclosure for chickens.
explanation.definitionFit: A run is a fenced pen where poultry are kept, the same thing as a coop for hens.

clue.text: Taking black bucket to feed horse

indicators.note: to feed means to go into the horse, as fodder goes into an animal's mouth

parts.note: a nag is an old or tired horse
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a bin is a container, a bucket for rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone takes a black bucket of feed out to a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabbing is informal for seizing or grabbing, a synonym of taking.

clue.text: Dad lost grand spoiling model

indicators.note: spoiling means ruining, so the letters of the phrase are ruined and rebuilt in a different order

explanation.surface: Dad lost a thousand pounds, spoiling a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' is slang for a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold standard is a benchmark of excellence by which others are judged, a model to follow.

clue.text: Empire collapsed with Republican leader

indicators.note: an empire that has collapsed has fallen to pieces, so its letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: An empire falls apart and a republican takes charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A premier is a prime minister, the head or leader of a government.

clue.text: Reception room contains worn-out bag

indicators.note: contains means the reception room word has the worn-out word sitting within it

parts.note: a hall is a large room used for receptions
old means worn out or shabby

explanation.surface: A reception room holding a shabby old bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A holdall is a large soft travelling bag that holds everything.

clue.text: Jewellery gives off metallic sound

definitions.meaning: bands of gold or silver worn on the finger
chimes like a bell when struck

explanation.surface: Jewellery that clinks and gives off a metallic sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Finger bands are pieces of jewellery, and a bell that chimes is said to do this, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Be excessively formal on deck

parts.note: over means on or above, as a coat goes over or on a shirt
to deck is to adorn or dress up

explanation.surface: Wearing formal dress on the deck of a ship, perhaps for a captain's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' suggests a ship; here it is the verb meaning to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdress is to wear clothes too smart for the occasion, being too formal in attire.

clue.text: Admirable French article, lines supporting former European politician

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means the lines sit below the rest, holding it up

parts.note: ex means former
MP is a Member of Parliament
la is the feminine form of the in French
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the lines

explanation.surface: An admirable French article about a former European politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Exemplary describes conduct so good that it serves as an example, worthy of admiration.

clue.text: Vegetable processed to get cure

indicators.note: processed food has been worked over, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A vegetable put through processing in order to cure it.
explanation.definitionFit: A courgette is a small marrow, a green summer vegetable known in America as zucchini.

clue.text: Suffer, short of energy

parts.note: under means less than, short of
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Suffering because of running low on energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to experience or endure it, to suffer it.

clue.text: Older relative with thing mostly for hard rock

parts.note: gran is a grandmother, an older relative

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: an item is a thing

explanation.surface: Granny, with a thing for hard rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard rock' suggests heavy music; it is a literal stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a very hard igneous rock used for building and worktops.

clue.text: Drink two times wiped from bed cover

indicators.note: wiped from means the two time letters are rubbed out of the bed and cover words

parts.note: a cot is a child's bed
a coat is a covering layer, as of paint
T is the abbreviation for time, so two times is two Ts

explanation.surface: A hot drink spilt and twice wiped off the bedspread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed cover' reads as a quilt, but it is two words: a bed (COT) and a cover (COAT), each losing one T.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate beverage, a classic bedtime drink.

clue.text: Near console on the blink

indicators.note: on the blink means faulty, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Getting close to a games console that is on the blink.
explanation.definitionFit: Close on is an idiom for almost or nearly, as in close on a hundred, so it means near.

clue.text: Secretive group is on top of termination in contract for player

indicators.note: in a down clue on top of means the earlier pieces sit above the final letter

parts.note: a cell is a small secret group within a larger organisation

indicators.note: termination means the end, so the last letter of contract is taken

explanation.surface: A secret group put the finishing touch to a contract for a player.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellist plays the cello, so is a musical player.

clue.text: Home female once worshipped somewhere in America

parts.note: in means at home
Diana was the Roman goddess of hunting, worshipped in ancient times

explanation.surface: A woman once idolised at home lives somewhere in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is a Midwestern state of the USA, so it is a place in America.

clue.text: Lost away from land

explanation.surface: Lost away from land.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means sailing on the ocean and, figuratively, bewildered or confused.

clue.text: Strolled from Post Office, post already despatched here and there

indicators.note: only some letters are sent on, every other one, scattered here and there through the words

explanation.surface: Someone walked from the Post Office after the post had already gone out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of 'post already': O, T, L, E, D.
explanation.definitionFit: To pootle is British slang for to move along in a leisurely way, so pootled means ambled or strolled.

clue.text: The Queen in Great Britain is keeping primarily little animals

indicators.note: in means the Queen's abbreviation goes inside Britain's

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

indicators.note: keeping means the word is holds a letter inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of little is taken

explanation.surface: The Queen in Great Britain keeps mainly small animals as pets.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerbils are small burrowing desert rodents often kept as pets, so they are animals.

clue.text: Studio set back in thoroughfare I let, affordable

indicators.note: set back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A studio flat set back from the main road, which I let out at an affordable rent.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's workshop, a French word for a studio.

clue.text: Maybe, Real and Inter with many out injured

indicators.note: injured means hurt or damaged, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Football clubs Real Madrid and Inter Milan have many players out injured.
explanation.walkthrough: Real and Inter look like football clubs, but the real is Brazil's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The real is the currency of Brazil, an example of a monetary unit, hence 'Maybe'.
